I tried to test ThorVG 0.15.0 and 0.15.1 to see if that was fixed but had some errors while building (probably because i just downloaded the source and copy-pasted in the directory in Godot source) so i'll let someone with more knowledge handle from there to check if that was already fixed or not.

As this is likely a ThorVG issue you can see if you have similar issues in the ThorVG web viewer https://thorvg.github.io/thorvg.viewer/ with the files and if so open an issue in https://github.com/thorvg/thorvg/issues for the ThorVG devs to look at.

[ThorVG web viewer](https://thorvg.github.io/thorvg.viewer/) successfully opens the SVG, which makes this issue more likely to be on Godot's side.

Also, today I was working on my game and noticed this other SVG ([click here to download as zip file](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17530359/up.zip)) which was successfully imported by Godot 4.3, even though it had an image, but a much smaller image than the buggy one.

Maybe the segmentation fault occurs because of the way ThorVG is implemented on Godot and not because of ThorVG specifically? Is there any way to see how much memory ThorVG uses during import and try to allocate give more memory to it?

If this integration between Godot and ThorVG become a very hard bug to solve with very little compensation for the effort invested in the solution, we can try to just put a warning when importing SVGs and some "try-catch" mechanism to prevent Godot from crashing when the segmentation fault occurs should be fine.

Sorry if I'm talking nonsense, I'm noob at C++.

@MDIVS You're right, the webview version works but the web view is the version 1.0.0 pre3, is a different version from the version in Godot

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/59195747-fbc2-4c1d-b48b-cc7229722766)

Is this still reproducible in 4.4.1-stable or 4.5-dev3?

I tested on Linux and can't reproduce on any Godot version, so this might only happen on Windows.
Tested on 4.5-dev3 on Windows 10, still crashes

I added a unit test which loads a jpg embedded in a svg, so assuming the unit tests run on the windows build automatically I'd be surprised if it isn't working now: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/104347/files#diff-35f139027358a7679eeceb2d301350a5a3766fb1a91e42f691839354323aee33R153

@BlueCube3310 Could you test again with 4.5-dev4 which includes #104347?

I tried with wine on Linux and it still crashes, but I'm not sure it's strictly related to this (I have a bunch of filesystem related errors).

I tested on v4.4.1.stable on macOS 15 and had no issues importing `hand_with_reference_image.svg` in the editor or loading it into an image using `Image.load_svg_from_string()` in a running project.

> Could you test again with 4.5-dev4 which includes [#104347](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/104347)?

I do not think this PR will make any difference as I don't think the Godot jpg importing process that the PR changes is involved in parsing jpg data embedded in SVGs, as that should be done inside ThorVGs parsing/rendering process. Maybe it's related to the similar SVG with embedded PNG issue: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/103876 that seems to have been fixed in ThorVG 0.15.12 (see https://github.com/thorvg/thorvg/issues/3327) that I think is used in 4.5-dev4?

> > Could you test again with 4.5-dev4 which includes [#104347](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/104347)?
> 
> I do not think this PR will make any difference as I don't think the Godot jpg importing process that the PR changes is involved in parsing jpg data embedded in SVGs, as that should be done inside ThorVGs parsing/rendering process.

It does, see the changes in that PR. ThorVG now uses libjpeg-turbo instead of `jpgd.h`.

> Maybe it's related to the similar SVG with embedded PNG issue: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/103876 that seems to have been fixed in ThorVG 0.15.12 (see https://github.com/thorvg/thorvg/issues/3327) that I think is used in 4.5-dev4?

It might be related but ThorVG was updated to 0.15.12 in 4.5-dev3, which still crashed for @BlueCube3310 on Windows.

Since you have no issue in 4.4.1.stable either on macOS, that confirms this is a Windows specific issue (possibly mingw bug).

Anyway, this is now confirmed fixed by #104347 in 4.5-dev4.
